strengths: deltaMic addresses a meaningful computer-vision problem: recovering explicit cell surfaces from volumetric fluorescence images without annotated training data. The mesh representation could support downstream geometric and biophysical analysis.

The combination of continuous surface rendering, analytic Fourier transforms and vertex gradients, CUDA acceleration, and PSF-dependent spectral truncation constitutes a concrete computational contribution. Figure 6 reports substantial acceleration over the CPU implementation.

The qualitative results are promising across synthetic shapes and mouse, ascidian, and worm microscopy. On 15 organoid images, Figure 9 reports improved rendering fidelity over DM3D, including MSE of 0.0020 versus 0.0125.
The manuscript provides a code-release reference, credits microscopy-data contributors and relevant methods, and acknowledges limitations involving spatially varying PSFs and computational cost.
weaknesses: The central claim of accurate shape inference lacks independent quantitative validation. Sections 6.2–6.3 evaluate rendered-image MSE, SSIM, and PSNR rather than surface accuracy, even though synthetic ground-truth meshes are available. Better image agreement does not establish correct boundaries, topology, or curvature, especially when blur is also adjustable. The real embryo results remain qualitative.

Joint geometry–PSF inference is insufficiently tested. Section 6.1 uses the same Gaussian PSF for synthesis and inference to isolate shape reconstruction, while the real experiments provide no calibrated PSF reference or quantitative parameter-recovery results. Consequently, the evidence does not establish whether optical parameters are recovered meaningfully or compensate for geometric and fluorescence-model errors. Robustness testing is also limited to one synthetic shape and a poorly specified noise model.

The incremental contribution needs clearer isolation. The paper acknowledges earlier mesh/PSF image fitting [31,64] and spectral geometry methods [37], but offers little direct comparison with these approaches. The DM3D experiment reuses its inferred meshes and evaluates renderings with deltaMic's inferred PSF, principally demonstrating refinement under the proposed image-fitting criterion. Controlled comparisons and component ablations would better establish the benefits of the new formulation.

Claims about eliminating shape regularization need qualification. Section 5.1 applies Laplacian-based gradient smoothing with λ = 50. This is distinct from adding a regularization penalty to the objective, but still imposes a smoothing bias on optimization. Without an ablation, smooth reconstructions cannot be attributed primarily to the optical model, and sensitivity to this parameter remains unclear.

Practical scalability and reproducibility are incompletely documented. Real reconstructions require 1,000–10,000 optimization steps, including full-spectrum computations for PSF updates, but end-to-end runtime and peak memory are not reported. Learning rates, detailed update scheduling, covariance constraints, and the noise-generation protocol are insufficiently specified in the supplied manuscript.

Several mathematical statements require correction: the Gaussian Fourier transform following Eq. (2) should use Σ rather than Σ⁻¹, and the linear system in Section 5.1 is not equivalent to the stated inverse-squared Laplacian update. These may be transcription errors rather than implementation failures, but should be reconciled with the code. They are secondary to the more consequential validation gaps above.
